title: Error handling is done better in production than in dev mode for Google fonts

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue was opened via the bug report template.

body:
### Verify canary release

- [x] I verified that the issue exists in the latest Next.js canary release

### Provide environment information

    Operating System:
      Platform: win32
      Arch: x64
      Version: Windows 10 Home
    Binaries:
      Node: 16.16.0
      npm: N/A
      Yarn: N/A
      pnpm: N/A
    Relevant packages:
      next: 13.1.1
      eslint-config-next: N/A
      react: 18.2.0
      react-dom: 18.2.0

### Which area(s) of Next.js are affected? (leave empty if unsure)

Font optimization (@next/font)

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/font/src/google/loader.ts#L198

### To Reproduce

Unable to reproduce active issue because I'm unable to reproduce the actual error - because I do not know of the actual error because of this error handling.

See this Stack Overflow question where this is relevant: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/74889692/next-js-example-takes-a-long-time-to-compile-due-to-inter-google-fonts
```
error - Failed to download `Inter` from Google Fonts. Using fallback font instead.
```

---

To mock an error, add `thisDoesNotExist();` after [line 107](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/font/src/google/loader.ts#L107).

### Describe the Bug

Next.js assumes that the error is of a specific reason despite the try statement runs through a massive 89 lines of code!!

When an error does occur, it assumes that it's because `fontFamily` could not be fetched from Google fonts, when this could be completely untrue!

Yet, it throws the actual error...when it's in production mode...

### Expected Behavior

Have the [actual error message](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/font/src/google/loader.ts#L223) output when it occurs in dev mode.
